notes: Translated from OVAL access_control/date1. Untranslated until 40b8ac6, because the permission had no target (IM 2.6.1); upstream added one in 531edf1 and made the policy a Set (c2773ed). The policy is now valid ODRL 2.2 and passes odrl22-shape.ttl; the rejection is due2's. The ODRL Information Model types no right operand, but due2-core binds odrl:dateTime with range xsd:dateTime, so a plain literal does not conform (due2-profiles.md §3). The literal also has no timezone, which XSD orders only partially (conformance/external/README.md finding 9), so typing it would not be enough: a dateTime right operand needs a timezone (decisions/0024). OVAL's request names no time, and OVAL reads the current time instead, so its answer depends on when it runs; due2's request always carries at (workflows §3.2). OVAL's result is kept in oval_expected; due2 evaluates no request.

expected_rejection.why: The right operand of the dateTime constraint on <http://example.com/policy:6161#print> is the plain literal "2020-03-11T11:33:10", outside odrl:dateTime's range xsd:dateTime. Normalisation rejects a right operand that does not conform to its operand's range (due2-profiles.md §3), so W1 rejects the policy in stage 2.

oval_expected.title: While the action does not match the permission, as the dateTime is not specified, the current time can be used instead to determine that a match would happen
